standard_citations.missing_diagnosis_support: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2024, Section I.B.1: Conditions that are not documented in the medical record by the provider must not be assigned.
standard_citations.code_diagnosis_mismatch: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2024, Section I.A.19: Code assignment is based on the documentation by the attending healthcare provider.
standard_citations.unspecified_code_usage: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2024, Section I.B.18: Sign/symptom/unspecified codes should be reported when a more specific diagnosis cannot be made. When a specific diagnosis is documented, the specific code must be selected.
standard_citations.duplicate_diagnosis: CMS Claims Processing Manual (Pub. 100-04) Chapter 23 §10: Duplicate or redundant diagnostic lines for the same encounter create claim adjudication errors and audit scrutiny.
standard_citations.unsupported_procedure: Social Security Act §1862(a)(1)(A) / CMS IOM Pub 100-02 Medicare Benefit Policy Manual Chapter 15 §20: No payment may be made for expenses incurred for items or services which are not reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of illness or injury.
standard_citations.missing_procedure_documentation: CMS 1995 & 1997 Evaluation and Management Documentation Guidelines / CPT Assistant: Every reported CPT code must be supported by complete documentation of the service rendered in the medical record.
standard_citations.incomplete_clinical_notes: Medicare Program Integrity Manual (Pub. 100-08) Chapter 3 §3.3.2.4: Medical documentation must contain sufficient clinical detail to support the level of care and medical necessity billed.
standard_citations.missing_provider_signature: CMS Medicare Learning Network (MLN) Matters MM6698: Medical record documentation requires a valid handwritten or compliant electronic signature by the authoring clinician.
standard_citations.high_level_em_underdocumented: AMA CPT 2024 E/M Guidelines & CMS 2021/2023 E/M Revisions: Level 5 office visits (99215/99205) require either high-complexity Medical Decision Making (MDM) or documented total time spent on the date of encounter.

severity_definitions.High: Potential compliance audit failure, overpayment risk, or critical medical necessity deficiency requiring mandatory human auditor review before claim submission.
severity_definitions.Medium: Documentation gap, missing element, or potential coding query candidate requiring review and possible provider addendum.
severity_definitions.Low: Informational coding optimization, unspecified code warning, or minor administrative discrepancy.
